chain.reading: no external record of a trigger exists: the operational channel is disabled on this host and the change that would enable it was refused without an elevated token
the run log records the process, and the scheduler's own register named the same instant while the witness was sampling

a witness process that is not the tick sampled the Task Scheduler's own reporting and it named this instant; this corroborates an engine launch, never the trigger type, because the channel that names the trigger is disabled
the internal identity of the run is recorded in the ledger entry of its slot
the slot's own outcome is recorded: a window was collected, or the slot was lost with a stated classification
the market evidence of the slot is referenced by hash and re-hashable from the window index

no_run_was_induced_for_this: no run was started by hand and none was forced outside a slot: a chain built from an induced run would prove nothing about the schedule
reason: the strongest chain this host can actually support is shown: the process, the run identity, the slot's outcome and its evidence are all held, and the scheduler's own register corroborates the launch — but the link that would make it a *scheduled* execution in Windows' own words is missing, because the operational channel is disabled and the request to enable it was not approved
requirement: WP-047-06 and the runtime test of RFC-047: show at least one real correlation between a Windows scheduled trigger, a process execution, an ST-6 run id, the outcome of the slot and the reference to its evidence
what_would_complete_it: enable the operational channel with an elevated token, let the schedule run, and read the channel again: a record naming this task's launch would move the slot's external state from PRE_ENABLE_NOT_OBSERVABLE to a confirmation, and the first link of the chain would carry its record id instead of a refusal
